Prunely Privacy Policy

Effective November 18, 2026 (version 1.0) · Last updated November 18, 2026

The short version. Prunely looks at your photo library on your iPhone and never uploads your photos. There is no account and we run no server for the app. Purchases go through Apple. There are no ads and no tracking.

Who we are

Prunely is made by an independent developer ("we", "us"). This policy covers the Prunely iPhone app, its widgets and Shortcuts. If you have a question, email SUPPORT_EMAIL_TBD.

Your photos

With your permission (Apple's Photos access prompt), Prunely reads your photo library so it can:

  • show your photos and videos as cards to keep, delete, favorite, skip or sort into albums;
  • measure file sizes, and find screenshots, large videos, Live Photos, bursts, duplicates, similar shots and blurry photos;
  • when you confirm, delete items, mark favorites or add items to albums in the Photos app.

All of this happens on your iPhone. Image analysis (finding similar or blurry photos) uses Apple's on-device frameworks. Your photos, videos, their contents and their metadata (dates, locations, faces) are never uploaded to us or anyone else.

Sharing your Recap. If you share your Recap card, Prunely creates an image of your stats, plus one favorite photo if you choose to include it (off by default), and iOS's share sheet sends it only where you share it.

If you choose Limited Access, Prunely only sees the photos you select. You can change access at any time in Settings > Privacy & Security > Photos > Prunely.

When you delete items, iOS shows its own confirmation, then moves them to the Photos app's Recently Deleted album, where they stay for up to 30 days before iOS removes them for good. Prunely never deletes anything without that confirmation.

Data stored on your device

To remember your progress, Prunely saves the following in its private storage on your iPhone:

  • your decisions (kept, staged for deletion, favorited, sorted), keyed by the Photos item's on-device identifier, with its size and date;
  • daily activity, goals, streaks and cleaned-space totals;
  • an image-analysis cache (numeric "fingerprints" and sharpness scores, not copies of your photos);
  • settings such as your daily goal, reminder time and pinned albums;
  • a small summary for widgets (for example "3.4 GB cleaned" and your streak), never photos or identifiers;
  • two numbers in your iPhone's Keychain recording how much you have deleted under the free allowance, so the allowance stays fair after a reinstall. This stays on your device (and in your own encrypted backups) and is not synced to iCloud Keychain.

This data never leaves your device except inside your own iPhone backups (iCloud Backup or a computer backup), which Apple and you control. We cannot access it.

iCloud Photos

Prunely has no iCloud sync of its own. If you use iCloud Photos with "Optimize iPhone Storage", some originals live in your iCloud. When you view such an item, iOS downloads it from your iCloud account to your iPhone, as the Photos app does. You can turn these downloads off in Prunely's Settings. We never see this traffic or your iCloud account.

With iCloud Photos on, deleting a photo also removes it from your other devices and any Shared Library. Prunely reminds you of this before you confirm.

Network connections

Prunely itself operates no server. The app connects to the internet only for:

  • Apple's App Store: loading prices, purchases, restores and subscription status.
  • iCloud Photos downloads, made by iOS as described above (optional).
  • Apple Maps place names (off by default). City names come from a list built into the app. If you turn on "Apple Maps place names" in Prunely's Privacy settings, the approximate center of each place group (an area about 20 km across, not a photo's exact location) is sent to Apple to look up its name. No photos are sent. Apple's handling is covered by Apple's Privacy Policy.

You can check this yourself with iOS's App Privacy Report (Settings > Privacy & Security > App Privacy Report).

Notifications and widgets

Reminders (daily tidy, trial-end reminder) are local notifications scheduled on your iPhone; they are not sent through any server. Widgets and Live Activities show totals such as space cleaned and your streak, read from your device. A Live Activity also shows the name of the deck you are tidying (for example an album or place name) on your Lock Screen. You can turn it off in Prunely Settings > Live Activity during a tidy.

Purchases and subscriptions

Prunely Pro is sold through Apple's App Store using StoreKit. Apple handles the payment, your payment details, your Apple ID and your billing address. We never see your name, email address or payment information. The app only receives a signed confirmation from Apple saying which product is active (for example, "Yearly, renews on a date" or "Lifetime") so it can unlock Pro. That check happens on your device. Apple's handling of purchase data is covered by Apple's Privacy Policy.

App Store Connect gives us aggregated, non-identifying sales reports (for example, how many trials started in a country). Apple does not give us your identity.

No ads and no tracking

This version of Prunely has no ads. It includes no advertising, analytics or tracking SDK, it never asks for permission to track you across other companies' apps and websites, and nothing you do in Prunely is used for advertising, by us or by anyone else. Prunely is paid for only by Prunely Pro, the optional yearly subscription and lifetime purchase.

If a future version adds advertising, we will update this policy, its changelog and the App Store privacy label before that version is released, and the app will ask for your permission where the law or Apple requires it.

What we never do

  • No account, sign-in or email address needed.
  • No uploading, scanning or "AI analysis" of your photos in the cloud.
  • No ads, and no advertising, analytics, tracking or crash-reporting SDKs.
  • We do not sell your photos or app data, and we never use them for advertising.

Data retention

  • On-device app data is kept until you reset it or delete the app (see below). We keep no copy.
  • Deleted photos stay in the Photos app's Recently Deleted album for up to 30 days, or until you empty it.
  • Purchase records are kept by Apple under Apple's policies.
  • Support emails you send us are kept only as long as needed to help you and keep a record of the conversation, then deleted, normally within 24 months. Ask us to delete them sooner at any time.

Deleting your data

  • Reset your progress: Prunely Settings > "Review everything again" clears decisions that haven't been committed.
  • Delete everything: delete the Prunely app. iOS removes its data, widgets and reminders. Only the two-number free-allowance counter in the Keychain remains on the device; it contains no photos or personal details.

Your privacy rights

Because Prunely has no account, no server and no ads, we do not hold a profile about you. Your app data is on your device. You can view, export (where the app offers it) and delete it yourself. Whatever your location, you can email us and we will help.

EEA, UK and Switzerland (GDPR / UK GDPR)

  • Who is responsible. We, the developer of Prunely, are the controller for the limited personal data we handle, which in practice means emails you send us. What you keep in the app stays on your device; we never receive it.
  • Legal bases. Replying to your support email: our legitimate interest in helping you (or steps you ask for before a contract). Purchases: handled by Apple under Apple's terms.
  • Your rights. Access, correction, deletion, restriction, objection and data portability, and, where processing is based on your consent, withdrawing it at any time without affecting earlier processing. Ask about any of them by emailing SUPPORT_EMAIL_TBD.
  • Complaints. You can complain to your local data protection authority. We would appreciate the chance to fix things first.
  • International transfers. Your app data is not transferred anywhere, because it never leaves your device. If you email us, your message is stored by the email service we use, which may be located outside your country.

California and other US states (CCPA / CPRA and similar laws)

  • What we collect. The app itself collects no personal information: what you enter stays on your device, is never sent to us, and there is no advertising, analytics or tracking SDK. If you email us, we receive your email address, what you write, and the app and iOS version that Prunely adds to the draft when you use Contact us in the app (you can delete them before sending). We use it only to reply.
  • No selling or sharing. We never sell personal information and never share it for cross-context behavioral advertising. We do not use or disclose sensitive personal information.
  • Your rights. To know/access, delete and correct the personal information we hold (in practice, your emails to us). We will not discriminate against you for using these rights. An authorized agent may make a request on your behalf with your written permission.
  • Retention. See Data retention.

Residents of other US states with consumer privacy laws (for example Virginia, Colorado, Connecticut, Utah, Texas and Oregon) have similar rights. Email us to use them. If we decline a request, you can appeal by replying to our answer with "Appeal" in the subject line.

Children

Prunely is rated 4+ on the App Store because it has no objectionable content, but it is a general-audience utility and is not directed at children under 13. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13 (or the equivalent minimum age in your country). If you believe a child has provided personal information to us, for example by email, contact us and we will delete it. Parents can prevent in-app purchases with Screen Time and Ask to Buy.

Security

Your app data is protected by iOS app sandboxing and Data Protection encryption on your device. Because we don't operate a server or collect your data, there is no developer-held database of your information that could be breached. No method of storage is perfect, so keep your device passcode and Apple ID secure.

Contact

Email SUPPORT_EMAIL_TBD for questions, privacy requests or complaints. If you email us, we receive your email address, what you write, and the app and iOS version that Prunely adds to the draft when you use Contact us in the app (you can delete them before sending). We use it only to reply. We usually reply within 2 business days and always within 7 days, and answer privacy requests within the time the law requires (30 days under GDPR, 45 days under CCPA).

Changes and changelog

If we change how Prunely handles data, we will update this page and the date at the top before the change takes effect, and for significant changes we will tell you in the app. The App Store privacy label is kept in line with this page.
